newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on El Nino, US crop worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on El Nino, US crop worries.

text.p: Worries that droughts produced by an El Nino weather pattern could cut into world rice output pushed CBOT rice futures higher at the close Tuesday, floor traders said.
"So far rains in India have been light and fragmented," said one rice trader.
On Tuesday, an offical with the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said that El Nino would likely produce drought in South Africa, Brazil and Australia.
Lingering concerns about the U.S. crop also underpinned prices, traders said.
"We've never had a spring this cool before," said one trader. "It's not going to be a record crop.
Traders also noted a decline in the condition rating of the U.S. crop. On Monday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said the crop was 10 percent excellent and 54 percent good.
Those figures compared with last week's ratings of 14 percent excellent and 50 percent good.
Rice closed three to 11-1/2 cents per cwt higher, with July up 11-1/2 at $11.485 per cwt.
Rice futures volume was estimated at 250 contracts, compared to the 272 traded Monday.
